hints: Use polynomial division, remembering that division by a quadratic leaves a remainder of degree at most $1$.
Divide $2x^4+0x^3+0x^2+0x-27$ by $x^2+x+3$, inserting the zero-coefficient terms to keep the powers aligned.
After each quotient term, subtract the whole product of that term and $x^2+x+3$; stop when the remaining expression is linear.
walkthrough: Set up polynomial long division for $(2x^4 + 0x^3 + 0x^2 + 0x - 27) \div (x^2 + x + 3)$:

Divide the leading term $2x^4$ by $x^2$ to get the first term of the quotient, $2x^2$:
$$2x^2(x^2 + x + 3) = 2x^4 + 2x^3 + 6x^2$$
Subtracting gives:
$$(2x^4 + 0x^3 + 0x^2) - (2x^4 + 2x^3 + 6x^2) = -2x^3 - 6x^2$$

Bring down $0x$ and divide $-2x^3$ by $x^2$ to get the second term of the quotient, $-2x$:
$$-2x(x^2 + x + 3) = -2x^3 - 2x^2 - 6x$$
Subtracting gives:
$$(-2x^3 - 6x^2 + 0x) - (-2x^3 - 2x^2 - 6x) = -4x^2 + 6x$$

Bring down $-27$ and divide $-4x^2$ by $x^2$ to get the third term of the quotient, $-4$:
$$-4(x^2 + x + 3) = -4x^2 - 4x - 12$$
Subtracting gives:
$$(-4x^2 + 6x - 27) - (-4x^2 - 4x - 12) = 10x - 15$$

Conclude with the quotient and remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = 2x^2 - 2x - 4$$
$$\text{Remainder} = 10x - 15$$

ai_rubric.Polynomial Division and Remainder Condit: Divides to derive a quotient of the form $2x^2\pm2x+k$ ($k\ne0$). Derives quotient $2x^2-2x-4$. Polynomial division gives quotient $2x^2-2x-4$. Remainder $10x-15$. Polynomial division gives quotient $2x^2-2x-4$; remainder $10x-15$.
